claims.disproof_condition: Downgrade if FY27 interim statutory reporting shows no growth in contract liabilities/customer advances despite the >10 reservation agreements described in August 2026, or if reserved volumes are cancelled/refunded; upgrade when any customer is named in a statutory filing (either side) or customer-side disclosure ties a reservation to Soitec.
claims.statement: Soitec's audited FY26 Universal Registration Document statutorily corroborates the capacity-reservation program: multi-year capacity reservation and volume commitment agreements signed with customers represent up to €1.1 billion in future sales at contracted prices (note 9.1, as of March 31, 2026), and non-current contract liabilities of €50.3m include €9,958k customer advances under multi-year sales contracts plus €40,330k related deferred income (note 8.14). This upgrades the August 2026 Reuters interview narrative to a regulated, audited disclosure and satisfies the 'statutory filing corroborates' half of the prior upgrade path. Limits: all counterparties remain unnamed; €1.1bn is a volume-commitment ceiling, not backlog or cash received; the customer-advance balance is slightly down year-on-year, so deposits from the agreements described in August 2026 are not yet visible on this balance sheet.

source_doc.title: Soitec 2025-2026 Universal Registration Document (AMF filed 2026-06-10, English courtesy translation)

sources.locator: Note 9.1 Commitments — Other trade obligations (printed p.279)
sources.quote: The Group has also signed various multi-year capacity reservation and volume commitment agreements with certain customers. These agreements represent a commitment for customers to purchase, and for the Group to supply, the allocated volumes as planned, which could represent up to €1.1 billion in future sales, based on the prices set out in these agreements.

sources.locator: Note 8.14 Provisions, other non-current liabilities (printed p.275)
sources.quote: Contract liabilities include: customer advances obtained under multi-year sales contracts amounting to €9,958 thousand (versus €11,200 thousand in the previous fiscal year); and deferred income of €40,330 thousand relating to contract liabilities under multi-year sales contracts, recognized as and when control of the goods and services concerned is transferred.
